questions.stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of a direct-mapped cache?
questions.explanation: A direct-mapped cache assigns each block of main memory to exactly one cache line, which can lead to higher conflict misses when multiple blocks compete for the same line. This is because if two frequently accessed memory blocks map to the same cache line, they will continually evict each other, causing more misses. The option of 'complex implementation' is incorrect because direct-mapped caches are actually simpler to implement than other cache types.

questions.stem: How does increasing the cache line size affect spatial locality?

options.text: It has no effect on spatial locality.

questions.explanation: Increasing the cache line size enhances spatial locality because it allows more contiguous data to be loaded into the cache at once. This means that when a program accesses data sequentially, the likelihood of the next piece of data being in the cache is higher. The option 'it decreases spatial locality' is incorrect because larger cache lines capture more of the surrounding data, improving spatial locality.

questions.stem: Explain the trade-offs between direct-mapped and set-associative caches.
markingGuide: Direct-mapped caches are simpler and faster.
Direct-mapped caches suffer from higher conflict misses.

questions.stem: What is the primary advantage of a set-associative cache over a direct-mapped cache?
questions.explanation: A set-associative cache reduces conflict misses compared to a direct-mapped cache by allowing multiple cache lines to be potential candidates for storing a memory block. This flexibility reduces the chance that two frequently accessed blocks will map to the same line and evict each other. The option 'simpler design' is incorrect because set-associative caches are generally more complex to design than direct-mapped caches.

questions.stem: Which factor does NOT affect cache performance?

These factors determine how efficiently data is stored and retrieved from the cache, whereas CPU clock speed affects the overall speed of processing instructions.

questions.stem: Discuss how cache pollution can occur with large cache lines.
markingGuide: Cache pollution occurs when unnecessary data is loaded into the cache.
Larger cache lines increase the likelihood of loading unused data.
This can reduce the effective cache capacity for useful data.
questions.explanation: Cache pollution happens when data that is not needed is loaded into the cache, occupying space that could be used for more frequently accessed data. Larger cache lines can exacerbate this issue by bringing in more contiguous data, some of which may not be used, thus reducing the cache's efficiency.

questions.stem: What does a cache hit indicate?

options.text: Data was found in the main memory.
Data was found in the cache.
Data was not found in the cache.
Data was found in the CPU registers.

questions.explanation: A cache hit indicates that the requested data was found in the cache, allowing for faster access than retrieving it from main memory. This is crucial for performance, as accessing data from the cache is much quicker than accessing it from main memory. The option 'data was found in the main memory' is incorrect because a cache hit specifically means the data was found in the cache, not in main memory.
